title: Where does logical element k live?
hints: Split the problem in two: turn `k` into one index per axis, then turn those indices into a buffer position.
Unravel from the last axis: `k % shape[d]` is the index on axis `d`, then divide `k` by `shape[d]` and move one axis left.
Add `index * strides[d]` for every axis on top of `offset`. Never assume contiguous: a stride can be 0 (broadcast) or larger than the shape suggests (permute or shrink).
explain: The reference walks the axes from last to first, peeling one index off `k` with `%` and `/`, and adds `index * stride` to `offset`. Because it uses the view's strides instead of assuming contiguous memory, permuted, broadcast and shrunk views all come out right.
